candidates.tagline: Sam Altman: having RAM in your PC is 'quite terrible' — it should be his
candidates.story: On November 2, 2026, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said on a podcast that it is 'quite terrible' for everyone to hold a share of the world's limited DRAM supply in personal computers where it sits idle most of the time, arguing all memory should be pooled in AI data centers — where OpenAI can charge you to use it.
candidates.why_funny: The CEO of a company that sells cloud AI subscriptions earnestly told the world that your personal RAM is a problem he would like to solve personally — by holding all of it, in his servers, for a monthly fee.
candidates.alt: Several black DDR5 G.Skill Trident Z5 CK Series memory sticks arranged in a row on a dark surface, their angular heat spreaders gleaming

candidates.tagline: OpenAI promised always-on AI agents for everyone; turned out they can't afford to run them
candidates.story: OpenAI launched 'Dots' in September 2026 — always-on AI agents with their own dedicated cloud computer to do everything for you 24/7 — but on November 3, 2026, OpenAI's head of ChatGPT admitted Dots are 'on the compute heavy side' and the company will route tasks to smaller, cheaper models; the same week, xAI throttled its own AI agents (Grok Bot) because costs were 'unsustainably high relative to revenue.'
candidates.why_funny: The entire AI industry promised personal agents that would run everything for you all day every day, then in the same week two major AI companies discovered they cannot actually afford to do that.
candidates.alt: Close-up photograph of the OpenAI custom Jalapeño inference chip developed with Broadcom, showing the semiconductor package on a circuit board
